h1: Mountain Creek Golf Resort — private pool villas inside a 27-hole mountain course in Sikhio
intro: If you want to escape the city to somewhere with nothing but the breeze and endless green fairways, Mountain Creek Golf Resort & Residences is a resort tucked into the hills of the Lam Takhong area, Si Khio district. It sits within the same grounds as a 27-hole championship golf course designed by the late golf legend Seve Ballesteros. The rooms are private pool villas — from the 65 sqm Winter Escape Deluxe up to the 250 sqm Spring Breeze Family with its own 10-metre pool. It's about 2 hours from Bangkok and just 10 minutes from Lam Takhong Lake. From approx. ฿2,400/night.

body.html: What sets Mountain Creek apart from the city hotels in Korat is the atmosphere. The resort sits on Mittraphap Road KM 91 in the Lam Takhong area of Si Khio district, on the same grounds as a 27-hole course designed by Seve Ballesteros, the legendary Spanish golfer. You're surrounded by hills and rolling green fairways, so quiet that many guests say it feels like stepping out of the outside world. The location suits people who genuinely want to relax, or golfers staying overnight by the course — far more than anyone hoping to wander markets or go shopping.

Accommodation here isn't a standard hotel room but villas, many of them with a private pool. They start with the Winter Escape Deluxe Villa at around 65 sqm, step up to the Summer Pool Villa at about 80 sqm with its own small pool, and reach the 250 sqm Spring Breeze Family Villa — two connected villas with 2 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and a 10-metre pool. The villas are decorated in warm tones with natural materials and plenty of space. Many guests praise them as clean, spacious and beautifully styled, with comfortable beds and deep sleep thanks to the quiet.
"Opened the curtains in the morning to green fairways as far as I could see, slipped straight into the private pool by the villa. So quiet you only hear the birds."

Beyond golf and the pool villas, the shared facilities include an outdoor pool, children's pool, spa and massage room, restaurant, bar, table-tennis room, karaoke and meeting rooms. The staff draw the most praise — reviews repeatedly mention how friendly, attentive and helpful they are, and Booking.com scores the staff category as high as 8.8. A golf-cart shuttle runs within the resort, since the grounds are large and some villas sit a fair distance from the main building. Breakfast, Wi-Fi and parking are all free.

For sightseeing, the resort is close to the nature of the Lam Takhong area. It's about 10 minutes' drive from Lam Takhong Lake and Dam, around 4 km from Muang Porn Garden, and on the route that continues to Khao Yai National Park or back into Korat city. It makes a tidy stopover for anyone driving up from Bangkok who wants to break the journey in a mountain setting. Overall scores sit around 8.0 on Trip.com and 7.8 on Booking.com, while TripAdvisor gives it 4.1 out of 5 and ranks it first among stays in the area.

Things to know before booking. As a resort that has been open for a while, parts of the buildings and the course show their age and need some upkeep — reviews mention patchy Wi-Fi in places, some flat pillows, and a course that in spots (especially in the rainy season) can be overgrown or have dried-out greens. A few in-room amenities aren't fully provided, and food and drink prices at the resort run high for the portions. Activities for children who don't play golf are limited too, so families with young kids should plan some outings nearby.

In short, Mountain Creek is a choice for anyone wanting a private pool villa in nature at a reachable price, or golfers who want to stay right by the course. You get quiet, space, hill views and genuinely warm service — in exchange for some dated corners, a reliance on the shuttle, and none of the shops or conveniences of the city. If your brief is a quiet retreat, a round of golf, or a stopover before Khao Yai, it delivers well in its own way.

A tip from following the reviews here for a while: if you're travelling as a family or group, the Spring Breeze Family Villa with its 10-metre pool works out better value than booking several separate rooms. Check the course condition with the resort first if golf is the whole point, especially in the rainy season. And expect some distance within the grounds — you can call the golf-cart shuttle any time, so there's no need to walk far.

faqTitle: FAQ — Mountain Creek Golf Resort, Nakhon Ratchasima

faq.q: Where is Mountain Creek Golf Resort and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's on Mittraphap Road KM 91, Lat Bua Khao, Si Khio district, Nakhon Ratchasima, in the Lam Takhong area, on the same grounds as a 27-hole golf course · about 10 minutes from Lam Takhong Lake and Dam · around 2 hours from Bangkok · roughly 1 hour on to Khao Yai National Park · about 50 minutes into Korat city.

faq.q: How much does Mountain Creek cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿2,400/night for the Winter Escape Deluxe Villa (approx. 65 sqm) · the Summer Pool Villa (approx. 80 sqm, small private pool) is around ฿3,500 · the 250 sqm Spring Breeze Family Villa with 2 bedrooms and a 10-metre pool is around ฿6,500 · prices move with season and holidays, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Mountain Creek have private pool villas?
faq.a: Yes · several room types are villas with a private pool, from the small pool in the Summer Pool Villa to the 10-metre pool in the Spring Breeze Family Villa · there is also a shared swimming pool and a children's pool on the resort grounds.

faq.q: Who is Mountain Creek best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for golfers who want to stay right by the 27-hole course, and anyone wanting a private pool villa in quiet, natural surroundings · also for drivers from Bangkok looking for a stopover before Khao Yai · less suited to those who want to walk to markets or expect city conveniences.

faq.q: What is the golf course at Mountain Creek like?
faq.a: It's a 27-hole championship course designed by Seve Ballesteros, the legendary Spanish golfer, set among the hills · praised for its views and challenge · note that in spots — especially the rainy season — it can be overgrown or have dried-out greens, so check the condition with the resort first if golf is the main reason for your visit.

faq.q: Anything to know before booking Mountain Creek?
faq.a: The resort has been open a while, so some corners are dated and need upkeep · reviews mention patchy Wi-Fi in places, a few amenities not fully provided, and high food prices at the resort · the grounds are large and rely on the golf-cart shuttle · plan some outings nearby if you're travelling with young children.
